words_and_claims_to_avoid: Government look-alike design, 'official notice', fake checks or invoices (39 USC 3001)
Unsubstantiated 'best', '#1', 'guaranteed savings', percent-savings claims (FTC Act s.5)
Invented or composite testimonials, star ratings or review counts (16 CFR 255)
'Free' unless it truly costs nothing and carries no hidden obligation
Fake expiration dates or fake scarcity; any deadline printed must be real
Demographic/age targeting language (e.g., 'seniors', 'retirees') unless the client has evidence it fits their actual buyers
Offering or advertising to pay, waive or rebate an insurance deductible (illegal in Texas without insurer consent; Florida bans incentives for inspections/claims)
'We'll handle your insurance claim / we work with your adjuster' style claims-advice (Florida: only licensed public adjusters may adjust claims)
'Storm reported in your area' unless a storm really hit that area
Lifetime/50-year durability claims unless backed by the manufacturer warranty terms (card 30 lesson)
'Do you qualify for a free new roof?', 'Your neighborhood has confirmed damage', 'Your neighbor reported storm damage' (eligibility/assertion framing; GOLD-roofing-021/022/056)
'Paid by your insurance' / 'Your insurance company may pay for a new roof' (GOLD-roofing-021/054) in FL/TX-style regimes; insurer decides coverage
Federal tax-credit claims on roofing products (e.g., '30% federal tax credit' on solar attic fans, GOLD-roofing-050): 25D ended for expenditures after 12/31/2025
'Value $X, savings Y%' unless $X is a real former price actually charged (GOLD-roofing-042; 16 CFR 233)
compliance_notes: If the sale closes in the home: FTC Cooling-Off Rule (16 CFR 429) applies to $25+ in-home sales; the client's contract must carry the 3-day cancel notice. States can add longer windows (e.g., California's 5-day window for buyers 65+ is documented for solar contracts).

Print the client's contractor license number where the state requires it in ads; requirements vary by state, and the client must confirm their own state's rule (we only verified the specific state rules named below).
Any discount must be off a real, recently charged price.

Texas Bus. & Com. Code 27.02: a seller commits a Class B misdemeanor by advertising or promising to pay, waive, absorb or rebate an insured's deductible without insurer consent; contracts of $1,000+ expected to be paid from insurance must carry a statutory 12-pt bold notice.

Florida Stat. 489.147: roofing contractors may not offer rebates, gifts, cash, coupons, deductible waivers or anything of value in exchange for a roof inspection or an insurance claim; written ads encouraging claims need specified warnings; violations carry fines up to $10,000 each. Practical effect: in Florida, do NOT pair 'free inspection' with a gift/discount framed around a claim. Client should confirm with counsel.
Storm/hail cards must not mimic government or insurer notices (39 USC 3001).

Reg Z, 12 CFR 1026.24 (verified): if a card states a down payment amount or %, the number of payments or repayment period (e.g., 'for 18 months', 'no payments for 12 months'), a payment amount ('$99/mo'), or a finance charge amount, it must also state the down payment, the full repayment terms and the 'annual percentage rate' using that term. Any rate (e.g., '0%') must be stated as an APR. Terms must be ones actually offered. Safe alternative: 'Financing available', which uses no trigger terms. Have the lender review.

FTC 'Free' Guide, 16 CFR 251 (verified): (1) 'free with purchase' means the paid item is at its regular price (sold openly for about 30 days), with no markup or downgrade to cover the free item; (2) all conditions go right next to the offer, not in an asterisk footnote; (3) if the main job is priced by negotiation or bid (typical for roofs, siding and window packages), 'free [item] with purchase' is improper; (4) don't run the same 'free' offer more than 6 months in any 12; (5) 'gift' or 'bonus' wording doesn't cure a deceptive 'free'.

Warranty ads, 16 CFR 239 + 702 (verified): 'lifetime/life' must say whose or what life (239.4); 'satisfaction/money-back guarantee' only if the full price is refunded on request, with conditions disclosed (239.3); advertise a warranty only if it is promptly honored (239.5). For consumer products over $15 with a written warranty, the terms must be available before sale; door-to-door sellers must tell buyers before closing that copies are available (702.3); ads should say where the full warranty can be seen (239.2).

2026-11-02 re-verification: FL 489.147 text unchanged in the 2026 Florida Statutes (last amended by ch. 2025-40). A 'prohibited advertisement' that encourages a roof-damage insurance claim must state, in 12-pt+ type at least half the size of the largest font: owner pays the deductible; deductible rebates/waivers are 3rd-degree-felony insurance fraud; filing a false claim is insurance fraud. No gift/discount/rebate in exchange for an inspection or for making a claim; no referral rewards; up to $10,000 fine per violation.

IRS (verified 2026-11-02): 25D residential clean energy credit is not allowed for expenditures made after 12/31/2025 (installation-completed date controls); 25C not allowed for property placed in service after 12/31/2025. Even before that, only the electricity-generating panel of a solar attic fan qualified (IRS Notice 2013-70 Q&A-29). Never print a federal tax-credit claim on 2026+ roofing cards.

Former-price/value claims (16 CFR 233.1): a 'value $9,000' or 'save 28%' comparison needs a real former price openly and actively charged for a reasonably substantial period. Roofs are bid-priced, so most 'value' anchors fail; use a flat '$[X] off' instead.
Named-storm specials (GOLD-roofing-046) are fine only if the storm actually hit the mailed area and the price is real; never imply official/FEMA affiliation.
standing_rules: Emotion-agnostic: fear, joy, pride, relief are all options; the client chooses.
Every angle carries a sell-the-outcome line.
Unverified (agency-only) results are labeled; never quote them as fact on a card.

emotion_by_offer_conflicts.conflict: Gold set and vendor pieces lead with financing (GOLD-roofing-011, MMR-578) vs Patrick hating financing-first cards 18 and 37
emotion_by_offer_conflicts.resolution: Patrick's votes win for headline placement because they are direct feedback on our output. The gold pieces show financing as a common offer, not that it works as a headline. Keep financing as a secondary offer under a problem or outcome headline. Re-test if votes change.

emotion_by_offer_conflicts.conflict: GOLD-roofing-002 'You qualify for a FREE roof inspection... may qualify for free insurance replacement' vs FL 489.147 and TX 27.02
emotion_by_offer_conflicts.resolution: Compliance wins. Don't use eligibility or 'free replacement through insurance' framing.

emotion_by_offer_conflicts.conflict: GOLD-roofing-007 'You have hail damage!' and 012 'STORM DAMAGE ALERT' vs FTC s.5 and 39 USC 3001
emotion_by_offer_conflicts.resolution: Compliance wins. Ask ('Did it hit your roof?') instead of asserting damage, and avoid official-alert styling.

emotion_by_offer_conflicts.conflict: Gold set and PostcardMania pieces show many pristine-house photos vs Patrick's 'just a nice house' feedback
emotion_by_offer_conflicts.resolution: Patrick wins for image choice. Show work or damage that matches the headline.

emotion_by_offer_conflicts.conflict: GOLD-roofing-021/022/054/056 eligibility and 'neighbor reported damage / paid by insurance' framing (common in new vendor samples) vs FL 489.147, TX 27.02, FTC s.5
emotion_by_offer_conflicts.resolution: Compliance wins. Ask a question ('Did last week's hail reach your roof?'), never assert damage, eligibility or insurer payment.

emotion_by_offer_conflicts.conflict: GOLD-roofing-050 '30% federal tax credit' (solar attic fan) vs IRS: 25D ended for expenditures after 12/31/2025
emotion_by_offer_conflicts.resolution: Law wins. No federal credit claims; at most 'ask about current state/utility programs' if the client verifies one exists.

emotion_by_offer_conflicts.conflict: Vendor ROI claims (GOLD-roofing-025-036, 017/018, 040) look strong vs no independent replication
emotion_by_offer_conflicts.resolution: Treat as agency-only unverified; use them to show which offers exist, not as proof. Patrick's votes and verified studies outrank them.
